Dusty Robotics

highlights: Prints coordinated layouts, labels and QR codes on the floor
Manufacturer specifies 1/16-inch layout accuracy
Single-operator workflow with Autodesk AutoCAD and iPad tools

The January 23, 2024 issuer announcement specifies a 23-pound mass including battery, approximately 10.43 kg. Its one-inch printhead and 300 dpi output are dated launch details; current support-page search previews were not imported as verified newer specifications.

The launch describes Edge Print near slab features, Shadow Print behind columns, curve printing, edge/obstacle sensing and Power Hold for battery changes. These named features do not establish exact edge clearance, uninterrupted battery runtime, charging duration or guaranteed fall/collision prevention.

The current platform combines robot, AutoCAD plugin, Dusty Portal and iPad operation. Its one-sixteenth-inch statement is layout-to-model accuracy with a coordinated/tracked workflow, not standalone robot pose accuracy or a guarantee that inaccurate surveyed control yields a correct building.

The October 19, 2026 Floor Elevation article says measurement is included in every package using the same robot and tracker. It describes live iPad heatmaps, point measurements, PDF/CSV exports and cloud stitching of multiple stations. An ASTM E1155 report remains something the customer or testing partner produces from the data, not an automatic certified output.

The PMD integration case study describes one motion-control drive per active front wheel, a passive rear wheel, IMU/encoder-assisted printing through occlusions, electronic braking and a communication watchdog. These supplier/engineer accounts are not independent safety certification or a universal blind-spot duration guarantee.

PMD’s compact single-axis drive and its electrical ratings are component specifications, not the robot’s body dimensions, power consumption or mechanical joint count. Engineer anecdotes about extreme weather do not establish formal FieldPrinter 2 operating limits or waterproofing.

Current pricing is based on utilization, platform access and implementation; included equipment covers the printer, tracker, iPad and joystick with operator/VDC training. No exact public price is established. North American availability and up-to-tenfold productivity are manufacturer statements, not worldwide stock or independently guaranteed output.

highlights: The June 15, 2021 issuer release identifies FieldPrinter as the first product and dates its first rollout to fall 2020. Earlier 2020 development and production accounts are distinct milestones, not proof of identical commercial hardware across all prototypes.

Dusty’s public post dated May 18, 2026 explicitly calls FieldPrinter 1 the original automated layout robot and announces it is retiring as FieldPrinter 2 takes over. This supports the historical generation name without inventing an exact final-shipping or end-of-support date.

The historical 2021 working guide requires at least three non-collinear surveyed control points and prepared CAD or CSV files. It distinguishes control accuracy from print placement and describes manual completion where access or tracker line of sight prevents robotic work. These historical requirements are not automatically FieldPrinter 2 specifications.

The founder’s November 2020 production account describes clutter, malfunctions, a backup robot and joint changes to site conditions and print scope. Reported schedule savings and the 2021 up-to-tenfold speed claim are contextual vendor/customer accounts, not guaranteed throughput or absence of rework.

The July 16, 2020 development blog names Amber as an internal second-generation platform. That wording predates the commercial FieldPrinter 2 announced in 2024; it does not establish that Amber is that later product or exactly identical to retired FieldPrinter 1. The codename remains a historical identity lead without an extra commercial robot card.

companyFocus.name: Dusty Robotics
companyFocus.role: Construction layout printing and floor-elevation workflow; historical first generation and current FieldPrint Platform
highlights: The issuer dates founding to 2018 and identifies Tessa Lau and Philipp Herget. First commercial FieldPrinter rollout is dated fall 2020; the manufacturer calls it FieldPrinter 1 in its May 18, 2026 retirement post. Commercial FieldPrinter 2 was announced January 23, 2024. Earlier internal Amber development terminology is not silently equated with that later product.

The FieldPrint Platform combines robot, external tracker, design plugins, Portal, iPad control and implementation. Current pricing describes utilization, platform access and training without a public numeric quote. North American availability does not establish worldwide supply or any specific customer’s current installation.

The native October 19, 2026 Floor Elevation article describes an included measurement capability using the existing robot/tracker, with live heatmaps and Portal PDF/CSV/cloud stitching. An older October 2024 press-index headline cannot establish all feature-version availability when its linked release is blocked. Floor Elevation and platform software are not additional hardware robots.

PMD’s integration account documents motion-control design with Dusty engineers; component footprint, electrical ratings and single-axis terminology do not become whole-robot ratings. Supplier accounts and marketing claims of highest accuracy, safety, savings or tenfold productivity are not independent proof of exclusivity or market leadership.

Three source hosts returned access denials and a deployment-owner article returned an explicit security block. Current support search previews, an unavailable manual mirror and the blocked release/deployment bodies are excluded as read evidence. Historical guide conditions, prototype lineage and present regional stock remain qualified; no portal, form, login or customer account was used.
